scope: Independent review of 9FD4's guarded 16-bit field update against original bytes and synthetic register memory. No physical device semantics are claimed.
checks: Reran all 240 original-byte cases in an isolated output directory; parsed replay rows match exactly.
The predicate is R0==1, unsigned R1<=1, and unsigned R2<65536. Valid rows read and write one word at 0x40010300+4*R1; invalid rows have no MMIO access and return 0x004A0001.
The pinned mask words at 0xA014 support preservation of bits 31..24 and 7..0 with R2 placed in bits 23..8. Fixtures cross boundary values and initial words 0, 0xA5A5A5A5 and 0xFFFFFFFF.
Every case preserves R4, restores SP, and has the expected raw return; accepted cases perform exactly one fresh read followed by one same-address word store.
limitations: The register window is synthetic. The trace does not establish physical peripheral meaning or concurrent update behavior.
The candidate is private P2 evidence only; caller reachability and canonical admission are outside scope.
